title: EE-107: vocabulary objects, shapes, and a parent check
body: One item of EE-107: nouns, verbs and kinds become vocabulary objects that other code can load, and a check can fail when something has no parent or does not match its shape. Writes, question routing, security labels, and wiring the rest of the tree are later items. ## Design Nouns stay in `docs/ontology.json`. Every field and relation there is unchanged. Verbs, kinds, tiers and declared shapes live in `schema/vocabulary.json`. `schema/vocabulary.ts` is the loader. It joins the two, and it refuses a verb or kind set that drifts from `design.diff.verbs` in `operations/operating-rules.json`, or a tier rule that drifts from `questions.impact`. Each object has a stable id: - A noun id is `noun:` plus the noun in lower case, spaces as hyphens. `venture` is `noun:venture`. `customer@finance` is `noun:customer@finance`. - Verbs are `verb:create`, `verb:amend` and `verb:delete`. - Kinds are `kind:originate`, `kind:derive`, `kind:append`, `kind:rename`, `kind:deprecate`, `kind:revise`, `kind:remove` and `kind:merge`. `derive` names its source. `merge` names its successor. A shape is a JSON Schema object. The checker enforces `type`, `const`, `enum`, `required`, `properties`, `additionalProperties`, string and number bounds, `pattern`, `items`, `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `if`/`then`/`else` and `not`. A keyword it does not enforce fails the load, so a shape cannot pass by being ignored. A noun with no declared shape has an open object shape. `noun:venture` declares a real shape. Every verb and kind declares the shape of a change line. The tier is the maximum of severity, reversibility, time to detect and blast radius. Each score is 1, 2 or 3, and that maximum selects `low`, `costly` or `one_way_door`. `tierOf` in the loader is that rule. This pull request does not apply the tier to writes. ## Parent The field is `vocabulary_parent`. - A record type sets it in `schema/data-model.json`. - A record sets the same field on itself. - A code module puts `// vocabulary_parent: ` in its first 40 lines. The shape check runs on instance records. A record type and a module are checked for a parent that resolves to a live object. A retired noun cannot be a parent. Wiring every record type, record and module is not built. The examples are the `venture` record type, `instance/ventures/everything-ecosystem/venture.json`, `schema/vocabulary.ts` and `schema/check-vocabulary.mjs`. ## Baseline `schema/vocabulary-baseline.json` lists subjects that have no parent yet. The check fails a subject that is not listed, fails a listed subject that now has a parent (the list has to shrink), and, once this file is on `framework`, fails an entry that was not in that copy unless the entry carries `approved` with who approved it and why. Shape mismatches are never baselined. This pull request is the starting ratchet: the file is not on `framework` yet, so these entries are the initial list. Counted on this checkout: | Population | Scanned | Named a parent | Baselined gaps | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Record types | 128 | 1 | 127 | | Core modules | 209 | 2 | 207 | | Instance JSON records | 56 | 1 | 55 | | Total | 393 | 4 | 389 | Core modules are `.mjs`, `.ts`, `.js`, `.cjs` and `.mts` under `schema`, `interface`, `knowledge`, `operations`, `evidence`, `governance`, `purpose`, `platform`, `packages` and `frameworks`, excluding tests and `schema/types/`. The two new modules name a parent, so the module gaps stay at the 207 that had none. Instance JSON files under `instance/` are 56 here. `node schema/check-vocabulary.mjs` runs the check. `node schema/check-nouns.mjs` runs it too, when the data model or the catalog is present, so the existing nouns step in CI covers it. `node test.mjs` also runs `schema/vocabulary-test.ts`. ## Tests `node test.mjs` passed, including schema validation, the noun check, the vocabulary tests and the type check. The vocabulary tests assert that a missing parent fails, a shape mismatch fails, a baselined gap passes, a new gap fails, removing a baseline entry is allowed once the gap is closed, and adding an entry fails unless it is explicitly approved. ## Next 1. Give every record type the noun it stands for, and tighten shapes toward the record schemas. That shrinks the 127 record-type gaps. 2. Put one change line (verb, kind, noun) on every write, and let `tierOf` decide whether the write lands, drafts or waits. 3. Route questions by verb plus noun plus asking function, with the standing-rule limits already in the operating rules. 4. Treat security as label nouns inherited through `derived_from`. Removing a label is an amend at `one_way_door`. 5. Clear the 207 module gaps and the 55 instance-record gaps as each file names a parent. 6. Let docs and READMEs read the loader. This pull request does not generate those docs.
